metadata_tags.NC_GLOBAL#source: The GEBCO_2026 Grid is the 2026 release of the  global bathymetric product published by the General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans (GEBCO) and has been developed through the Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 Project. This is a collaborative project between the Nippon Foundation of Japan and GEBCO. The Seabed 2030 Project aims to bring together all available bathymetric data to produce the definitive map of the world ocean floor and make it available to all.
metadata_tags.NC_GLOBAL#summary: The GEBCO_2026 Grid is a continuous, global terrain model for ocean and land with a spatial resolution of 15 arc seconds.The grid uses as a base-map Version 2.8 of the SRTM15+ data set (Tozer et al, 2019). This data set is a fusion of land topography with measured and estimated seafloor topography. It is augmented with gridded bathymetric data sets developed as part of the Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 Project.

interpretation: The local soundings are sampled at about 10 m, whereas EMODnet is about 100 x 115 m and GEBCO is about 400 x 460 m at Anza; those grids cannot resolve the local survey detail.
EMODnet DTM elevations are referenced to LAT according to the official product documentation; the downloaded GeoTIFFs do not contain a vertical-reference tag.
The GEBCO GeoTIFF metadata identifies elevations relative to mean sea level; GEBCO cautions that some shallow-water source cells may use another vertical reference.
GEBCO TID source classes intersecting the survey are summarized by distinct raster cell in gebco_tid_source_classes.csv; they describe coarse grid provenance, not each local sounding.
The EMODnet current and 2022 rasters have matching grids. Their differences are edition/revision discrepancies and must not be interpreted as seabed change.
Port Agadir ZH, EMODnet LAT, and GEBCO MSL are distinct references here. Do not merge elevations until their local/date-specific vertical ties are established.
The official 2024 IHO value for Agadir ZH relative to NGM is recorded separately; it is not applied to the 2022 survey.
